item.title: Ocean Mixing Barrier Shown: Dye experiment maps slow downward transport; layered structure limits exchange
item.description: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: New Zealand cat control helps endangered southern dotterels rebound 52% in one year
item.description: New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel population has risen by 52 percent following focused predator control efforts. Intensive campaigns targeting feral cats on Stewart Island have yielded immediate gains in breeding. The population grew from 105 birds in early 2025 to an estimated 160 in April 2026. Wildlife officials stress that ongoing management of feral cats is crucial for the bird's long-term survival. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Protests in Europe: Fact-checking viral videos amid claims of 'chaos'
item.description: As young people protest poor school conditions and the rising cost of living across Europe, misleading videos are spreading online.
